verdict.rationale: Databricks documents Structured Streaming and Auto Loader as streaming ingestion paths. Delta Lake tables serve as streaming sinks with exactly-once guarantees, and Real-Time Mode claims end-to-end latency as low as five milliseconds, which covers the core of low-latency streaming writes into tables. However, the evidence never states that sink data becomes queryable within seconds, and it shows no push-style ingestion endpoint for external producers. missing for 10: explicit documentation of query freshness on landed streaming data, a documented direct push/streaming ingestion API for external clients, independent or hands-on corroboration of seconds-level queryability

support.subject: As a data-engineer, streaming writes land queryable within seconds through a documented streaming ingestion API

citations.quote: Use Delta Lake tables as streaming sources and sinks with exactly-once processing guarantees.
RTM processes records as they arrive, with end-to-end latency as low as five milliseconds.
Structured Streaming lets you express computation on streaming data in the same way you express a batch computation on static data.
Incrementally and efficiently process new data files as they arrive in cloud storage.
